The brief's '9 headings/instructions' counts the citation among them. No Friday heading target exists, which matches integrated-assembly-review: 'n340 opens Friday (no printed heading)'.

Every target matches the final configuration. All wording selectors use the renamed slugs: veorekh/veomeq, sovev/sovel, haroim/reim, beriatekha/melakhtekha, az/af and khol/kheli. None says main_reading or alternate_reading. The slugs follow the transliteration table. The opening-psalm contexts are rerooted to siddur:hosafot/shir_hakavod/opening_psalm. The Wednesday L24 rule has the outer condition …/levaddo_hu_veniflaot_gedolot/optional and the inner one …/divine_name, with canonical_part null. The Sunday closing payloads (literal and realization) both carry divine_names ["ה׳"], so none of the 31 is stale.

Divine-name directive (source_encoding.py:154-176): it accepts only a list of nonempty strings. It searches only the text and tail slots of tei:body, excluding text already inside j:divineName (on a tail, only ancestors are checked, which is correct). It needs exactly one slot to match and exactly one occurrence in that slot. It splits the text into before + name + after, so the characters don't change and nothing is expanded. Matches are collected before anything is changed, and a name marked by an earlier list entry is excluded from later searches. This meets RC5's markup-only requirement.

Directive caveats, not blocking: (a) matching is by substring with no word boundary, so the only protection is the exactly-one rule plus the reviewed payload; (b) the tests cover the positive case, two occurrences in one slot ('ambiguous') and an empty string, but not zero matches, two occurrences in different nodes (that error says 'requires exactly one matching element', not 'ambiguous'), a non-list value, or exclusion of an already-marked name; (c) RC5's second clause, about tei:abbr/tei:expan when abbreviations are expanded, is left out on purpose, so expanded builds will show ה׳ abbreviated; (d) the review hash covers the serialized config, not the directive's code, as source-encoding-code-final.json already notes.
